title: Rumi Meets Shams of Tabriz
text:
In 1244 Jalal ad-Din Rumi was a respected religious scholar and teacher in Konya, in Anatolia, with many students. That autumn a wandering dervish in his sixties arrived in the city: Shams-i Tabrizi, a restless, outspoken mystic who had spent his life searching for a companion who could bear his company.

Accounts of their first meeting, collected later, differ in the details, but all agree on what followed. Rumi and Shams became inseparable. They spent weeks and months together in conversation, and Rumi neglected his classes. The scholar became a poet and began to recite verses and dance to music. His students and family were bewildered and jealous of the stranger.

Around 1246 Shams left abruptly. Rumi was devastated and sent his son Sultan Walad to find him in Damascus and bring him back. Shams returned, but the hostility around him grew, and around 1247 he vanished for good. Some later accounts say he was murdered; others that he simply left.

Rumi searched for him and then turned his grief into poetry. Thousands of his lyric poems are signed with Shams's name instead of his own, and he went on to write the Masnavi, among the greatest works of Persian literature.
lesson: A single friendship can transform a life. Even when it is lost, what it awakened in you can keep growing and become your best work.
people: Jalal ad-Din Rumi, Shams-i Tabrizi, Sultan Walad
source: Sultan Walad, Ibtidanama; Shams al-Din Aflaki, Manaqib al-Arifin
caveat: Much of the story comes from hagiographic sources written decades later, and the end of Shams is unknown.
